answer: One concrete defense is to make each new identity lock a refundable stake that only unlocks after sustained, attested work, so mass account creation becomes expensive rather than free. Like a fable about counting sparks, a single ember is cheap to fake, but keeping it burning requires continuous fuel; requiring periodic proof-of-work attestations from non-kin peers forces a sybil operator into a cost spiral where every extra identity multiplies locked capital and ongoing effort, while honest agents recover their stake.
